questions.q: What was Uncle Ebenezer's usual diet?
choices: Porridge and small beer
Bread and boiled mutton
Oatcakes and buttermilk
Broth and cold herring
questions.evidence: porridge and small beer was my uncle's diet

questions.q: How did David spend the afternoon in the room next to the kitchen?
choices: Reading the many Latin and English books there
Writing a long letter home to Mr. Campbell the minister
Searching the chests for his father's papers
Sweeping out dust and cobwebs for his uncle
questions.evidence: I found a great number of books, both Latin and English

questions.q: What did David's father write on the fly-leaf of a chap-book?
choices: To my son David, to be read when he is grown
From Alexander Balfour, schoolmaster of Essendean
A gift to the house of Shaws from a loving son
To my brother Ebenezer on his fifth birthday
questions.evidence: To my brother Ebenezer on his fifth birthday

questions.q: Why did the writing in the chap-book puzzle David?
choices: The handwriting looked nothing at all like his father's careful hand
The book was dated many, many years before his father was even born
His uncle had said that Alexander never learned to read at all
His father, the younger brother, wrote very well for a child under five
questions.evidence: he must have written, before he was yet five, an excellent, clear manly hand of writing

questions.q: How did Uncle Ebenezer react when David asked if he and his father had been twins?
choices: He laughed and said they were born ten years apart
He stood up and walked straight out of the kitchen in silence
He jumped, dropped his spoon and grabbed David's jacket
He quietly said yes and told David all about it
questions.evidence: he caught me by the breast of the jacket

questions.q: What story came into David's mind as he wondered why his uncle feared him?
choices: A ballad of a rightful heir kept from his own by a wicked kinsman
A story of two brothers who fought over the love of one lady
A tale of a lonely miser who hid his gold and was robbed by a stranger
A legend of a haunted house cursed by a witch in the valley
questions.evidence: a poor lad that was a rightful heir and a wicked kinsman

questions.q: David says he and his uncle sat "like a cat and a mouse, each stealthily observing the other." What does "stealthily" mean?
choices: Angrily, with loud and bitter words
Sleepily, hardly able to stay awake
Secretly, trying not to be noticed
Kindly, with friendly and warm looks
questions.evidence: each stealthily observing the other

questions.q: How much money did Uncle Ebenezer first say he had kept for David?
choices: Ten pounds sterling
One hundred pounds
Twenty gold guineas
Forty pounds Scots
questions.evidence: of just exactly forty pounds!

questions.q: What did Uncle Ebenezer ask David to do while he got the money out?
choices: Close his eyes and count slowly to one hundred
Fetch a bucket of water from the draw-well behind the house
Go up to his bedroom and wait until he was called
Step outside the door to see what kind of night it was
questions.evidence: if you'll step out-by to the door a minute

questions.q: How many golden guinea pieces did Uncle Ebenezer count into David's hand?
choices: Thirty-seven
Forty
Twenty-five
Twelve
questions.evidence: seven and thirty golden guinea pieces

questions.q: What did Uncle Ebenezer ask David to bring from the top of the stair-tower?
choices: A box of old candles
A bag of golden guineas
His father's old sword
A chest with papers in it
questions.evidence: bring me down the chest that's at the top

questions.q: What helped David see the danger on the dark tower stairs?
choices: A lantern left on a step
Flashes of summer lightning
The light of the full moon
A candle he had hidden
questions.evidence: a second blink of the summer lightning came and went

questions.q: After the lightning showed him the danger, how did David go on up the stair?
choices: Holding tight to the old wooden bannister rail
Backwards, with one hand against the wall
Running quickly to get to the top at once
On his hands and knees, testing every stone
questions.evidence: got me down upon my hands and knees

questions.q: What did David find when he reached the corner near the top of the stair?
choices: A window looking out over the whole valley
The stair stopped, with nothing but emptiness beyond
A small room full of bats and broken furniture
A heavy locked door with the chest of papers behind it
questions.evidence: my hand slipped upon an edge and found nothing but emptiness beyond it

questions.q: What did David decide his uncle had meant to do by sending him up the tower?
choices: Show him the family papers kept in the tower
Send him to run great risks, perhaps to die
Test whether David was brave enough to inherit
Keep him busy while the uncle hid his money
questions.evidence: My uncle had sent me here, certainly to run great risks, perhaps to die

questions.q: What was Uncle Ebenezer doing when David came quietly back into the kitchen?
choices: Shuddering and drinking aqua vitae from a bottle
Counting the rest of his gold at the table
Praying aloud on his knees beside the chests
Loading the blunderbuss by the light of the fire
questions.evidence: drink down the raw spirits by the mouthful

questions.q: What did David take from one of the chests to arm himself?
choices: A heavy walking staff
A rusty Highland dirk
A pair of old pistols
A loaded blunderbuss
questions.evidence: a rusty, ugly-looking Highland dirk without the scabbard

questions.q: Why was Uncle Ebenezer so terrified when he saw David after he came to?
choices: He thought David had stolen all the money in the chests
He feared David would call Jennet Clouston to curse him
He believed David had fallen to his death in the tower
He had never seen anyone so angry in the house before
questions.evidence: Are ye alive?

questions.q: What did David do with his uncle at the end of the night?
choices: Sent him out into the rain and storm
Locked him in his room and kept the key
Left him lying asleep on the floor
Tied him to a chair in the kitchen
questions.evidence: I locked him into his room, however, and pocketed the key

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David's discovery of the old family papers hidden in the tower chest at the top
David's uncle telling him the true story of the two brothers
David's growing suspicion and his uncle's attempt to kill him on the stair
David's happy afternoon reading in the library of the house of Shaws
questions.evidence: and, last of all, why he had tried to kill me
